title: Take ownership of one recurring activity
why_matters: You become part of the team's load when you take something off someone else's plate. Owning a recurring activity — a meeting, a report, a stand-up segment — is the cleanest way to do this. Pick something small enough that you can do it well; visible enough that ownership is noticed.
steps: List two or three recurring activities you've watched someone else do for the last six weeks (e.g., weekly status report, retro facilitation, sprint refinement note-taking).
Pick the one where (a) you have the context, (b) the current owner would be relieved, (c) you can sustain it for a full month.
Ask the current owner if you can take it. Frame it as you wanting the reps, not them wanting the relief.
Do it. Send the first week's output back to the previous owner for sanity-check.
success_criteria: You have publicly taken ownership of one recurring activity. The first iteration under your ownership has been sent. The previous owner has acknowledged the hand-over.
reflection_prompt: What was easier than you expected, and what was harder?
